# Loopiter

> A lightweight, model-agnostic feedback loop for production AI systems.

Loopiter is an MIT-licensed software development kit for Node.js 22 and 24 and for Python 3.11+. The libraries capture executions and feedback, analyze scored segments, evaluate immutable candidates, and coordinate approval, deployment, or rollback through adapters the application owns. The default mode stores recommendations. Autonomous changes require an explicit opt-in and a complete policy. The policy validator accepts only an exact prompt or routing target. The Node validator also accepts agent_release. Python does not. Loopiter is a library, not a hosted service, a model, a trainer, or an agent runtime. The core has no runtime dependencies and sends no telemetry. Current alpha: npm `0.3.0-alpha.1`, Python `0.3.0a1`. The landing page introduces the SDK. A hosted console is separate from this library.

Source code: https://github.com/SanaanKhalid/loopiter

## Pages

- [Home](https://loopiter.co/): SDK console, the feedback loop, graduated autonomy, and links to the manifesto and blog.
- [Manifesto](https://loopiter.co/manifesto): Why a useful correction should start an improvement attempt, and what the application still decides.
- [Blog](https://loopiter.co/blog): Notes on evaluation and feedback loops.
- [Evaluate self-improving AI agents offline before they change production](https://loopiter.co/blog/evaluate-self-improving-ai-agents-offline): How the repository’s Node offline KB-QA benchmark compares a frozen baseline with the SDK autonomous loop. Train is the optimization split, dev is validation and audit, and a held-out test is scored only after the loop. The harness uses seeded mocks and records zero live model calls. It checks a validation rejection, an observation rollback, and simulated spend caps. The printed scores are mocked, not a measurement of a real model.
- [Self-improving AI agents need a feedback loop you can evaluate](https://loopiter.co/blog/self-improving-ai-agents-need-a-feedback-loop-you-can-evaluate): What self-improving agents change, why an outside check matters, and which parts of that loop this SDK implements. Links to the offline benchmark note.

## Documentation

Canonical documentation is hosted separately from this site.

- [Overview](https://loopiter.docs.buildwithfern.com/get-started/overview): Capture, verified feedback, evaluation, approval, deployment, and rollback.
- [Supported capabilities](https://loopiter.docs.buildwithfern.com/get-started/supported-capabilities): What the Node.js and Python alphas include, and what they leave to the application.
- [Opt-in autonomous improvement](https://loopiter.docs.buildwithfern.com/closing-the-loop/opt-in-autonomous-improvement): Observe, recommend, experiment, and autonomous modes.
- [Evaluation and deployment](https://loopiter.docs.buildwithfern.com/closing-the-loop/evaluation-and-deployment): Immutable candidates, holdout partitions, receipts, and rollback.
- [Agent systems](https://loopiter.docs.buildwithfern.com/closing-the-loop/agent-systems): Recording turns and tool calls without treating the SDK as an agent runtime.
- [Fine-tuning boundaries](https://loopiter.docs.buildwithfern.com/closing-the-loop/fine-tuning): The alpha does not train or fine-tune a model.
